headline: Brazil Central Bank Holds Selic Rate at 13.75% Amid Inflation Concerns
summary: Brazil's central bank unanimously kept the Selic rate at 13.75% in November, pausing its rate-cut cycle due to rising uncertainty and inflation expectations.
why: The Selic is Brazil's benchmark interest rate, setting the baseline for borrowing costs across the economy and influencing fixed-income yields and equity valuations.

impacts.name: Selic rate
impacts.why: The central bank voted to maintain the benchmark Selic rate at 13.75%.
impacts.baseline_rule: first recorded price at or after created_at (15-minute price recorder); end = first price at least 24 h later, within 48 h

why_moved: Maintaining elevated interest rates anchors monetary policy but increases financial burdens on indebted companies and consumers, prompting mixed reactions in local markets.
